title: The localizing category is locally small with split idempotents
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\Lambda$ be one of the condensed coefficient rings listed, with its coefficient data and topology, in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Work with small sites and sums in the fixed universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The full subcategory $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ of $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ defined in [sk-def-localizing-closure] is locally small and triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], has arbitrary small direct sums, and has split idempotents: for every $e:K\to K$ with $e\circ e=e$, there are an object $J$ of this subcategory and maps $i:J\to K$, $p:K\to J$ in it with $i\circ p=e$ and $p\circ i=\mathrm{id}_J$.

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda_X$, $\mathcal A=\Mod_R(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab))$ and $\mathcal T=D(\mathcal A)$ as in [sk-def-localizing-closure], on the small site skeleton of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with coefficient values in the common larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The coefficient rings listed there are commutative; [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] makes $R$ a commutative ring object of abelian sheaves. The tensor and strong monoidal abelian sheafification are those of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. In particular sheafification carries tensor products of local equivalences to isomorphisms, because its tensor comparison identifies their images with tensor products of isomorphisms. Thus the size, sheafification and monoidality hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] hold. Apply its equivalence to $R$. It identifies $\mathcal A$ with sheaves of modules over the reconstructed section ring sheaf, whose multiplication is $(r,s)\mapsto\mu(r\otimes s)$ and whose unit is $\eta(1)$, preserving underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restriction maps identically. Denote this ring sheaf again by $R$. The coefficient ring object has stayed the actual pulled-back condensed ring throughout.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified tensor and bilinear universal property; existing internal-abelian-sheaf-module equivalence and pulled-back coefficient definitions

proof.text: Use the small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with coefficient values and indexing sets in the same larger universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. The theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to this small site and its sheaf of rings $R$, so its category $\mathcal B$ of sectionwise left $R$-module sheaves is Grothendieck abelian. Write $F:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$ for step 1's equivalence. Its unchanged underlying abelian sheaves make it additive. For any diagram in $\mathcal A$, the Hom bijections of $F$ identify its cocones with the cocones of its image; applying a quasi-inverse to the colimit in $\mathcal B$ consequently gives its colimit in $\mathcal A$. For a morphism $f$, a quasi-inverse image of $\ker(Ff)$ is a kernel of $f$: the Hom bijections identify arrows annihilated by $f$ with arrows annihilated by $Ff$, and identify their unique factorizations through these objects. A quasi-inverse image of $\operatorname{coker}(Ff)$ is a cokernel of $f$, since the Hom bijections also identify arrows annihilating $f$ and their unique factorizations. The canonical coimage-to-image map becomes an isomorphism in the abelian category $\mathcal B$; since an equivalence reflects isomorphisms, $\mathcal A$ is abelian. Thus exact sequences are detected by $F$, and the exactness of filtered colimits in $\mathcal B$ proves exactness in $\mathcal A$. If $G$ is a generator of $\mathcal B$, then for unequal maps $f,g$ in $\mathcal A$ choose a map $G\to F(\operatorname{dom} f)$ distinguishing $Ff,Fg$ and use the Hom bijection to get a distinguishing map from a quasi-inverse image of $G$. Hence $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian in that universe. By [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], every unbounded complex in $\mathcal A$ has a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism into a K-injective complex; no constructibility, boundedness or completeness assumption is used.

For $K,L\in\mathcal T$, choose representing complexes $N,M$ using the localization description [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a K-injective resolution $M\to I$ supplied by step 2. Since $QM\cong QI$, the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives
$$\Hom_{\mathcal T}(K,L)\cong\Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(N,I).$$
The right side is a set in the fixed universe: chain maps form a subset of $\prod_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Hom_{\mathcal A}(N^n,I^n)$, and chain-homotopy classes form a quotient of that set. Here each sheaf-module Hom is itself a subset of the product of sectionwise maps over the small site; the module values, the site skeleton and $\mathbf Z$ have the common size fixed in step 2. If the localization was initially formed in a larger universe, this bijection provides its small Hom sets. Thus $\mathcal T$ is locally small. The subcategory $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ is full by [sk-def-localizing-closure], so its Hom sets are precisely these ambient Hom sets.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), displayed Hom equality; derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), assertion (3)

proof.text: The ambient $\mathcal T$ is an additive triangulated category with integer shifts and the cone triangles described in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian by step 2, apply [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]: for any small family of representing complexes $(N_a)$, the termwise sum complex $\bigoplus_aN_a$ represents a coproduct of $(QN_a)$ in $\mathcal T$. Every derived object has a representing complex, so $\mathcal T$ has all such coproducts, including the empty and countable sums.

source.place: Tag 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), assertions (1)-(2); triangulated structure as in derived.tex Tag 05RR

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal L=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Its defining object predicate in [sk-def-localizing-closure] is membership in every full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and closed under small ambient sums. The ambient $\mathcal T$ itself is one such subcategory by step 4. The zero object, shifts, cones and isomorphic replacements of objects of $\mathcal L$ lie in every subcategory in this definition, and hence in $\mathcal L$. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], the full subcategory on this predicate has the induced triangulated structure. For any small family $(L_a)$ in $\mathcal L$, its ambient sum from step 4 belongs to every defining subcategory, hence to $\mathcal L$. For each $B\in\mathcal L$, fullness identifies
$$\Hom_{\mathcal L}(\bigoplus_aL_a,B)=\Hom_{\mathcal T}(\bigoplus_aL_a,B)\cong\prod_a\Hom_{\mathcal T}(L_a,B)=\prod_a\Hom_{\mathcal L}(L_a,B).$$
The bijection is given by the ambient coprojections, which are morphisms of $\mathcal L$ by fullness. Thus these ambient sums are sums in $\mathcal L$, including the zero object for the empty family.

source.place: Triangulated with sums paragraph; intersection definition in sk-def-localizing-closure/_section.md; derived.tex Tag 05QM

proof.text: By step 5, $\mathcal L$ is in particular pretriangulated, has a zero object, the additive integer shifts inherited from the ambient derived category, and countable coproducts. Apply [lem-countable-coproducts-idempotent-complete] to $\mathcal L$ itself. It says that this category is idempotent complete. Consequently, for every $e:K\to K$ in $\mathcal L$ with $e^2=e$, its splitting object $J$ and splitting maps $i:J\to K$, $p:K\to J$ lie in $\mathcal L$ and satisfy $ip=e$, $pi=\mathrm{id}_J$, as required. Applying the theorem inside $\mathcal L$ ensures that the splitting is internal to the localizing closure.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported three-paragraph argument into six steps. Identified internal modules over the actual pulled-back condensed ring with modules over its ring sheaf before applying the existing Grothendieck theorem; computed small Hom sets via the existing K-injective resolution and Hom-comparison nodes; proved inheritance of the ambient triangulation and coproduct universal property by the intersection definition; applied the existing countable-coproduct idempotent-completeness node inside the localizing category. Clarified the implicit scheme and indexing universe in the statement, without changing the coefficients or conclusion. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. Second reading uses the existing internal-abelian-sheaf-module equivalence, verifies its monoidal-sheafification and commutative-ring hypotheses, and writes out preservation of the Grothendieck axioms through that equivalence.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the locally-small paragraph by steps 1-3, the triangulated-with-sums paragraph by steps 4-5, and the idempotents paragraph by step 6 of main-20261015 sk-lem-brown-hypotheses-ambient.proof.md; these are the ambient part of step 1 of unit sk-lem-brown-hypotheses.
